1800:
**Ἐνώς** (Heb. אֱנוֹשׁ), ὁ,
Enos (Gen.4:26): Luk.3:38.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1801:
** ἐνωτίζομαι**,
(οὖς) **give ear, hearken to,** λόγους {{LXX+NT|LXX.Gen.4.23; ῥήματα NT.Act.2.14: with _dative_, ἐντολαῖς LXX.Exo.15.26.}}
1802:
**Ἐνώχ** (Heb. חֲנוֹךְ), ὁ,
Enoch (Gen.5:18): Luk.3:37, Heb.11:5, Ju 14.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1803:
** ἕξ**,
**οἱ**, **αἱ**, **τά**, _indeclinable_, **six,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.270, +others: _dative_ _plural_ ἑξάσιν “OGI” 200.28 (from Axum)}}; ϝέξ {{Refs|“Tab.Heracl.” 2.34, +others, “GDI” 1267.27 (Pamphyl.), 4968 (from Gortyn): ἓκ ποδῶν is written in “IG” 12.372.175}}; compare ἕκπους.
**2** ἕξ, τό, **the six** in ἀστράγαλοι used as dice, ={Κῷον}, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus “Oss.” 38}}. (Cf. Sanskrit _[snull]á[tnull]._ Avest. **xšvaš,** Latin _sex,_ Welsh **chwech,** etc.)
1805:
** ἐξᾰγορ-άξω**,
**buy from,** τι παρά τινος {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.42.2}}; **buy up,** {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Crassus” 2}}; **buy off,** μικροῦ διαφόρου τὸν ἀδικηθέντα {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Dicaearchus Geographus 1.22}}; **redeem,** {{NT+1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 36.2; ἐκ τῆς κατάρας τοῦ νόμου NT.Gal.3.13}}:—_middle_, ἐξαγοράξεσθαι τὸν καιρόν {{LXX+NT|NT.Col.4.5, cf. NT.Eph.5.16 (but -άζειν τὸν κ. LXX.Dan.2.8).}}
1810:
** ἐξαίφν-ης**,
_adverb_ **on a sudden,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.738, 21.14, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.52, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1077 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1610, etc.: with}}_participle_, ψυχὴν θεωρεῖν ἐ. ἀποθανόντος ἑκάστου **the moment that** he is dead, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 523e}}; ἀκούσαντι ἐ. **at first** hearing, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|[prev. author] “Cra.” 396b: with _Article_, τό γ᾽ ἐ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.153}}; but τὸ ἐ. **the instantaneous,** that which is between motion and rest, and not in the time-series, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 156d}}; but, ={τὸ ἐν ἀναισθήτῳ χρόνῳ διὰ μικρότητα ἐκστάν}, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 222b15.}}
1812:
** ἑξᾰκόσι-οι**, αι, α,
**six hundred,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.51, etc.}}: _Doric dialect_ **ϝεξακάτιοι** {{Refs|“Tab.Heracl.” 2.41.}}
1818:
** ἐξᾰπᾰτάω**,
_Epic dialect_ _iterative_ ἐξαπάτασκον {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1070 (hexameter)}}:—_passive_, _future_ **-απατηθήσομαι**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 499c}}; but -απατήσομαι in _passive_ sense, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.3}}:—**deceive** or **beguile, deceive thoroughly,** εἴτινά που.. ἔτι ἔλπεται ἐξαπατήσειν {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.371, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.414, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.29, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.153, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 901, etc.; ἐ. τινὰ φρένας [prev. author] “Pax” 1099 (hexameter); ἐ. καὶ φενακίζειν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.204}}; **seduce** a woman, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.114: with double _accusative_, ἐ. τινά τι}} **in** a thing, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.1.19; also ἐ. ἐπὶ τοῖς ἰδίοις συμβολαίοις 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 10.7}}; περὶ σαυτὸν ποιεῖσθαι.. ἐφ᾽ οἷς ἐξαπατᾷς ἔλεον surround yourself with compassion for your **swindling tricks,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.196}}; ἐ. τινὰ ὡς.. **cheat** him **into believing** that.., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.7.6, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 413d}}; ἐ. νόσον **beguile** or **assuage** it, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nigr.” 7}}:—_passive_, ὡς ἐξαπατηθείς {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.94; ἐνόμιζον ἐξηπατῆσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.42; ᾔδει ὑπὸ τῆς μητρυιᾶς ἐξαπατωμένη 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.19; τὸ δεῖπνον ἐξαπατώμενος 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 60; ἐ. ἀπάτην 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 2.9.6}}:—_middle_ like _active_, _falsa lectio_ in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 439c.}}
1819:
** ἐξάπῐν-ᾰ** [ᾰπ],
later form of ἐξαπίνης, {{LXX+NT+2nd c.AD+|LXX.Num.4.20, NT.Mark.9.8, “PGiss.” 1.68.6 (2nd c.AD), 6th c.AD: Procopius Caesariensis Historicus “de Aedificiis” 2.11}}.
1820:
** ἐξαπορέω**,
strengthened for ἀπορέω, to be in **great doubt** or **difficulty,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.34.1; τοῖς πράγμασι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 23.1}}:—_middle_, ἀπορούμενοι, ἀλλ᾽ οὐκ ἐ. {{NT|NT.2Cor.4.8}}: so in _aorist_ _passive_ ἐξηπορήθην {{LXX+1st c.BC+|LXX.Psa.87(88).15, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 24.1, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alcibiades” 5}}; ἐξαπορηθῆναι ἀργυρίον **to be without** money, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 7.18; τῶν κοινῶν ἐξηπορημένων “SIG” 495.12 (Olbia, 3rd c.BC),compare “PEleph.” 2.10 (3rd c.BC).}}
1823:
** ἐξαστράπτω**,
**flash as with lightning,** {{LXX+NT|LXX.Nah.3.3, NT.Luke.9.29}}; of the sun's light, Zos.Alch.{{Refs 5th c.BC+|p.111 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus; φόβῳ καὶ κάλλεϊ 3rd-4th c.AD: Tryphiodorus Epicus 103.}}
1824:
** ἐξαυτῆς**,
_adverb_, for ἐξ αὐτῆς [τῆς ὁδοῦ], **at once,** {{NT+6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 231, 5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 34, 4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 22.29, 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 641, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.7.7, NT.Mark.6.25, “POxy.” 64.3 (3rd-4th c.AD), etc.}}
1828:
** ἐξέλκ-ω**,
_future_ **-έλξω**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 365 (Pors.)}}: _aorist 1_ -είλκῠσ; _infinitive_ **-ελκύσαι**{{Refs|[prev. author] “Pax” 315, 506}}:—_passive_, **-ελκυσθῇ**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.70}}:— **draw, drag out,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.762: with _genitive_ loci, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.432 (_passive_)}}; φάσγανον.. ἐ. κολεοῦ {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 544}}; Ἑλλάδ᾽ ἐ. δουλίας **rescue from** slavery, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 1.75}}; δύστηνον ἐ. πόδα, of a lame man, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 291: _absolutely_, without πόδα}} of one wounded, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1121; ἐξέλξω σε τῆς πυγῆς θύραζε 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 365 (Pors. for ἐξελῶ)}}; ἐξελκύσαι τὴν πᾶσιν Εἰρήνην φίλην **drag** her **out of the** cave, {{Refs|[prev. author] “Pax” 294, compare 315, 506}}; rare in Prose, as {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 515e; ἐξελκυσθείς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1311b30; τέχναι τινὰ ἐ. τῆς πενίας 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 39.14.}}
1830:
** ἐξερευν-άω**
(later **ἐξερευν-έραυν-** {{LXX|LXX.Psa.118(119).2, +others)}}, **search out, examine,** {{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 258, “El.” 1100; τὰ περὶ τὴν πόλιν 4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 28.4; λογισμὸς τὰς αἰτίας ἐ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 3p.64U.; τὰς προσόδους 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 14.1.13, cf. LXX [same place], +others; τὰ πρόσφορ᾽ ἤν πως ἐξερευνήσας λάβω 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 429}}:—_middle_, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 52.6; τόπους 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 9.5.8, compare 18.21.1.}}
1832:
** ἔξεστι**,
_imperative_ ἐξέστω, _subjunctive_ ἐξῇ, _infinitive_ ἐξεῖναι, _participle_ ἐξόν: _imperfect_ ἐξῆν: _future_ ἐξέσται, _optative_ ἐξέσοιτο {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Agesilaus” 1.24}}_participle_ ἐξεσόμενον (see. below): _impersonal_ (see. ἔξειμι B):—**it is allowed, is possible,** with _infinitive_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.183, etc.}}: with _dative_ _person_ et _infinitive_,{{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. work] 138, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 899, etc.; ἔ. σοι ἀνδρὶ γενέσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.1.21; ἔ. εὐδαίμοσι γενέσθαι}}**'licet esse beatis',** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 3.23}}: with _accusative_ instead of second _dative_, ἔ. ὑμῖν φίλους γενέσθαι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.20}}: with _accusative_ _person_ et _infinitive_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1079, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 290d: _neuter_}}_participle_ _absolutely_, ἐξεόν τοι.. ἕτερα ποιέειν **since it was possible** for thee to.., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.126; ἐξόν σοι γάμου τυχεῖν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 648; ἐξὸν κεκλῆσθαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 365; ὡς οὐκ ἐξεσόμενον τῇ πόλει δίκην.. λαμβάνειν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.10.}}
1835:
** ἑξήκοντα**
(ϝεξ- {{Refs 5th c.BC+|“SIG” 56.30 (Argos, 5th c.BC))}}, οἱ, αἱ, τά, _indeclinable_, **sixty,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.587, etc.}}; οἱ ἑ., a college of γελωτοποιοί at Athens, Telephan. cited in {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 14.614d.}}
1841:
** ἔξοδος**, ον,
**B** **promoting the passage,** λίθων {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “χρονίων νούσων θεραπευτικόν” 2.3.}}
1842:
** ἐξολεθρ-εύω**,
**destroy utterly,** {{LXX+NT+1st c.AD+|LXX.Gen.17.14, +others, NT.Act.3.23, variant in 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 8.11.1. (The spelling -ολοθρ-}} in this group of words is frequently in later codices and Papyrus, as {{Refs 6th c.AD+|“PMasp.” 2 iii 28 (6th c.AD).)}}
1845:
** ἐξορκ-ιστής**, οῦ, ὁ,
**exorcist,** {{NT+2nd c.AD+|NT.Acts.19.3, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “epigram” 23, 2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 182.}}
1848:
** ἐξουθεν-έω**,
={ἐξουδενόω} {{LXX+NT+1st c.AD+|compare (οὐ σὲ ἐξουθενήκασιν, ἀλλ᾽ ἢ ἐμὲ ἐξουσενώκασιν LXX.1Ki.8.7), LXX.Wis.4.18, +others, NT.Luke.23.11, NT.Rom.14.10, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 6.5.4.}}
1852:
** ἐξυπν-ίζω**,
(ὕπνος) **awaken from sleep,** οἱ κόρεις εὐχρήστως -ίζουσιν ἡμᾶς {{NT+3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Chrysippus Stoicus 2.334, cf. NT.John.11.11}}:—_passive_, **wake up,** {{LXX+1st c.AD+|LXX.Judg.16.14, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Antonius” 30, 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 6.31. (Condemned by 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 200, etc., uncertain in “Comica Adespota” 43.)}}
1853:
** ἔξυπν-ος**, ον,
**awakened out of sleep,** ἔ. γενέσθαι {{LXX+NT+5th c.BC+|LXX.1Esd.3.3, NT.Act.16.27, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 11.3.2, Zos.Alch. p.118 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus}} _adverb_ **-νως**{{Refs 2nd c.AD+|“PGiss.” 1.19.4 (2nd c.AD).}}
1857:
** ἐξω-τέρω**,
_adverb_, _comparative_ of ἔξω, **more outside,** δρόμου ἐ. {{LXX+4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 1023, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1055a25, LXX.Job.18.17, etc.}}:—hence later, _adjective_ **ἐξώτερος**, **outer,** {{LXX+NT+4th c.AD+|LXX.Exo.26.4, etc., NT.Matt.8.12; ξυστός “POxy.” 896.14 (4th c.AD).}}
1865:
** ἐπαθροίζομαι**,
_passive_, **assemble besides,** {{NT+1st c.AD+|NT.Luke.11.29, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Antonius” 44.}}
1866:
** ἐπαιν-ετός**, ή, όν,
**to be praised, praiseworthy, laudable,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 416c, “Lg.” 660a, etc.; τὸ ἐ.}}**the object of praise,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1101b13}}: _comparative_, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD(?): Theon Rhetor “Progymnasmata - Rhet.” 12}}. _adverb_ **-τῶς**{{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ ποιημάτων” 2.26, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.682, +others}}
1874:
** ἐπακρο-άομαι**,
={ἐπακούω}, _absolutely_, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 16, 1st c.BC: Nicolaus Damascenus Historicus “Vita Caesaris” 29: with _genitive_ _person_, NT.Act.16.25, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Icar.” 1: with _genitive_ _of things_, 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 2.17: with _accusative_ _of things_, πάντ᾽ ἐπακροάσει 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Epit.Oxy.” 1236v16}}; τὸν λόγον Ant. {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista 11.6}} **ἐπακρό-ᾱσις**, εως, ἡ, **hearkening, obedience,** {{LXX|LXX.1Ki.15.22.}}
1878:
** ἐπανα-μιμνῄσκω**,
**remind** one **of, mention again to** one, τινά τι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 688a, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Memoria” 451a12, 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Abstinentia - Porphyrii Opuscula” 1.30; ἕκαστον ὑμῶν, τίς.. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 6.35.}}
1882:
** ἐπανόρθ-ωσις**, εως, ἡ,
**setting right, correcting,** τᾶς ψυχᾶς {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 104b; κόλασις εἰς - σιν φέρουσα 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 2.80c; ἐδεσμάτῶν Diocl.fragment 138}}; **revision,** νόμων Legal cited in {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 24.22}}; ἐ. ἔχειν to be capable of **improvement,** opposed to ἀνίατον εἶναι, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1165b18}}; of circumstances, **amendment,** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.66.12, 1.11.2, etc.}}
1887:
** ἐπαύριον**,
_adverb_ **on the morrow,** τῇ ἐ. ἡμέρᾳ {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“PLille” 1.15 (3rd c.BC)}}; ἡμέρα ἡ ἐ. {{LXX|LXX.Num.11.32; usually τῇ ἐ.}}**on the morrow,** {{NT+3rd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.53.6, +others, NT.Matt.27.62, +others; εἰς τὴν ἐ. 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 8.13.6, +others (Sts. written ἐφ-, “PHamb.” 1.27.4 (3rd c.BC), “PTeb.” 119.17 (2nd c.BC).)}}
1889:
**Ἐπαφρᾶς**, -ᾶ (B1., § 7, 4), ὁ,
**Epaphras**: Col.1:7 4:12, Phm 23.*†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
1897:
** ἐπείπερ**
or **ἐπεί περ,** see at {ἐπεί} {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1, 2, 5.}}
